pages.title: Irish Elk
pages.text: The Irish elk ($(o)Megaloceros giganteus$()), or giant deer, is an extinct deer that lived across Eurasia, from Ireland to Siberia, during the Pleistocene and earliest Holocene.$(br2)Despite its name, it was neither exclusively Irish nor an elk; its closest living relatives are the fallow deer.$(br2)Males carried the largest antlers of any known deer, spanning up to 3.6 metres from tip to tip.
